sections.label: Goods and people between countries
sections.summary: More than S$80 billion of goods and 200 million people cross between the two countries yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: More than S$80 billion worth of goods and 200 million people traverse between our two countries each year.

sections.label: HSR KL-Singapore connection
sections.summary: The HSR, set to operate in 2026, will give a 90-minute city-to-city link between KL and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The HSR, scheduled to be operational in 2026, will provide a 90-minute, city-to-city connection between KL and Singapore.

sections.label: RTS Link capacity and start
sections.summary: The RTS Link operates from 2024 and can move up to 10,000 passengers per hour each direction.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The RTS Link will be operating from 2024 and has the capacity to move up to 10,000 passengers per hour in each direction, about two-thirds of the peak-hour traffic between Johor and Singapore.

sections.label: Joint tender for AssetsCo
sections.summary: Infrastructure Companies from both countries are preparing a joint tender for the HSR Assets Company by year end.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The two Infrastructure Companies from both countries are preparing to call a joint tender for the HSR Assets Company, or "AssetsCo", by the end of the year.

sections.label: LTA licence non-compliance penalties
sections.summary: Clause 39 lets LTA suspend or cancel a licence or impose a penalty up to one million Singapore dollars or 10% of annual revenue.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In the event of non-compliance, clause 39 empowers LTA to suspend or cancel a licence, or to impose a financial penalty of up to one million Singapore dollars or 10% of the licensee's annual revenue, whichever is higher.

sections.label: Obstructing rail safety inspectors
sections.summary: Obstructing a rail safety inspector or independent safety auditor is an offence, punishable by a fine up to $5,000 or six months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Any person who obstructs the rail safety inspector or independent safety auditor in carrying out his or her duties shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $5,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months.

sections.label: LTA as railway security agency
sections.summary: LTA is to be appointed as the cross-border railway security agency under the Bill, given its experience securing Singapore's public transport system.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Given LTA's experience in ensuring the security of the public transport system in Singapore, we intend to appoint LTA as the cross-border railway security agency under this Bill.

sections.label: Arms and Explosives Act amendments
sections.summary: The Arms and Explosives Act will be amended to extend powers to enforcement officers to arrest without warrant persons committing dangerous offences and enforce cross-border railway security.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The Arms and Explosives Act will also be amended to extend powers to enforcement officers under this Bill to arrest without warrant persons committing dangerous offences, to enforce security of the cross-border railway at all times.

sections.label: Legislative support for HSR and RTS
sections.summary: The Bill provides legislative support for the construction, management and operation of the proposed KL-Singapore HSR and the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It provides legislative support for the construction, management and operation of both the proposed KL-Singapore HSR and the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS.

sections.label: MPA share transfer requirements
sections.summary: The Bill introduced onerous share transfer requirements, obliging a person becoming a 5% controller of a designated entity to notify MPA and seek prior approval for 25%, 50% or 75% or indirect controller status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In that Bill, we saw the introduction of onerous share transfer requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There is an obligation for a person becoming a 5% controller of a designated entity to notify the MPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A person will also need to seek the prior approval of MPA before becoming a 25%, 50% or 75% controller or an indirect controller of a designated entity.

sections.label: Equity controls for concessionaires
sections.summary: For the same reasons argued in the MPA (Amendment) Bill debate, the same equity controls provisions must apply to all concessionaires, operators, subcontractors or licensees at all times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For the same reasons as the Government has argued in the recent debate for the MPA (Amendment) Bill, surely the same equity controls provisions introduced in the MPA Act must also apply to all concessionaires, operators, subcontractors or licensees at all times or there will be some inconsistency.

sections.label: Two months' notice for owners
sections.summary: Under clause 8(3), owners must be given at least two months' notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under clause 8(3), owners must be given at least two months’ notice.

sections.label: Notice period for property
sections.summary: The speaker calls the provision unfair for commercial and residential property and asks the Government to reconsider a notice period of at least six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Whether it is a commercial property or a residential property, this is equally unfair.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will reconsider this provision to give a longer notice period of, say, at least six months.

sections.label: Auditing railway maintenance regimes
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify whether the Independent Safety Auditor and rail safety inspectors will audit or inspect railway and associated infrastructure maintenance regimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Minister please clarify whether the Independent Safety Auditor and the rail safety inspectors will also be auditing or inspecting the maintenance regimes of the railway and associated infrastructures?

sections.label: Objection to railway area delineation
sections.summary: The speaker says clause 6, which provides no right of objection to delineation of land as railway area, should be reconsidered or amended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In that regard, clause 6, which provides that no person has a right of objection to the delineation of land as railway area, should be reconsidered or amended.

sections.label: Timelines for Malaysia projects
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Minister is confident both countries can meet projected construction and launch timelines, and whether Malaysian General Elections may affect progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On the issue of meeting timelines, as the projects also substantially involve Malaysia, and quite heavily so, is the Minister able to tell this House whether he is confident that both countries will be able to abide by the projected timelines for construction and launch of the projects?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Should we be concerned at all whether the outcome of the next Malaysian General Elections may have any effect on the progress of the projects?

sections.label: HSR line under private land
sections.summary: The speaker raises public feedback and says it is currently unclear if the HSR line will run under any privately-held land in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I only have three quick points of clarifications to raise, based on feedback from the public, and similar to some of the points that Mr Dennis Tan had raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that it is currently unclear if the HSR line will run under any privately-held land in Singapore.

sections.label: EIA results and security agency
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether EIAs will be conducted before HSR construction and made public online, and notes clause 58 designates a cross-border railway security agency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will EIAs be conducted before the construction of the HSR line and will the results of such EIAs be made public and available online?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, under clause 58, a "cross-border railway security agency" will be designated.

sections.label: CBR Bill terms
sections.summary: The CBR Bill will set out terms for construction, maintenance, operations and regulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The CBR Bill will set out the terms for the construction, maintenance, operations and regulation.

sections.label: HSR terminus and second CBD
sections.summary: The HSR terminus is the focal point for the second CBD in Jurong Lake District, supporting close to 200,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: The HSR terminus is also the focal point, as Members may have already known, for the development of our second Central Business District (CBD) in Jurong Lake District, which can support close to 200,000 jobs.

sections.label: Each country appoints InfraCo
sections.summary: Each country will appoint an Infrastructure Company to build, fund, own and maintain civil infrastructure within their countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: First, each country will appoint an Infrastructure Company, or InfraCo, to build, fund, own and maintain the civil infrastructure within their respective countries.

sections.label: AssetsCo tender preparations
sections.summary: Singapore and Malaysia are in final preparations and will call the AssetsCo tender by the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Singapore and Malaysia are in the final stages of preparations and will be calling the AssetsCo tender by the end of the year.

sections.label: Fares and rail safety audits
sections.summary: Both countries agreed fares will be set commercially by train service operators and not regulated, and rail safety auditors will audit maintenance regimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In addition, both countries have agreed that fares will be set commercially by respective train service operators and will not be regulated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: The rail safety auditors will also double up to audit the maintenance regime of the entities.

sections.label: Co-located CIQ facilities
sections.summary: Both countries agreed that HSR and the RTS Link will offer co-located Customs, Immigration and Quarantine facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Both countries have agreed that HSR and the RTS Link will offer co-located Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) facilities.

sections.label: Suspension of cross-border railway services
sections.summary: Singapore can suspend cross-border railway services in emergencies and inform Malaysia and private entities without seeking their concurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In the event of, for example, a terrorist attack or natural disaster, Singapore can suspend cross-border railway services in Singapore and take necessary follow-up measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Singapore will inform Malaysia as well as any private entities involved about the suspension of services but is not required to seek their concurrence before doing so.

sections.label: Environmental impact assessments and public feedback
sections.summary: Proposed local lines, HSR and RTS Link will undergo EIA, with information provided to the public and feedback invited via a hybrid Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Each line locally that we are proposing will undergo the EIA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Likewise, for the HSR and RTS Link, we will undergo the same process as per our domestic lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: When ready with the engineering studies, we will be providing the necessary information to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In fact, we will be looking at this as a hybrid Bill and invite public feedback for further consideration.
